description: Radxa ROCK 5C (Rockchip RK3588S2) dev board, on order. A board record: Atlas flashes it from maskrom (rockusb) with Rockchip's loader file and no vendor tool. Written from rkdeveloptool, U-Boot and Radxa's docs; untested on this board.

storage_target_evidence: docs.radxa.com ROCK 5C introduction: one eMMC module connector (no module fitted by default) and a microSD slot; no SPI flash.
The image is a whole disk as Gaia writes it for eMMC (idblock at sector 64, U-Boot, partitions), written from byte 0.
instructions: Power the ROCK 5C off and take out any microSD card; fit the eMMC module.
Short the Maskrom pin hole with a DuPont wire (the ROCK 5C has no Maskrom button).
Connect the top USB 3.0 port (the OTG port) to this computer, then power the board on and remove the wire.
The board appears as 2207:350b (RK3588 maskrom). Atlas runs the loader's DDR init and usbplug, writes the image to the eMMC, reads it back and restarts the board.
todo: 2207:350b as RK3588 maskrom comes from secondary sources (MNT, Radxa's guides via search); confirm with lsusb on the board.

Whether the RK3588S2 takes the RK3588 loader unchanged: rkbin's rk3588_loader_v1.24.114.bin, Radxa's rk3588_spl_loader_v1.15.113.bin (both names match); Gaia's board build copies it next to the image.
The cable: Radxa's guides differ between USB-A to USB-A and USB-A to USB-C for this port.
Which polynomial the loader's trailing CRC-32 uses (0x04C10DB7 as in rkdeveloptool's table, or 0x04C11DB7): Atlas accepts either and logs which.
